findings.title: Changing span buffer keys from sets to sorted sets breaks existing Redis data during rollout
findings.body: Span buffers are stored at `span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id`. Before this change those keys are Redis sets; this diff starts writing them with `ZADD` and later calls `ZCARD`/`ZSCAN`/`ZUNIONSTORE` (`buffer.py` lines 197 and 434, plus `add-buffer.lua`). During a rolling deploy, any old set key touched by the new consumer, or any old consumer touching a new zset key, will get a `WRONGTYPE` error. Existing keys have a TTL up to `redis_ttl` (default 3600 seconds), so affected batches can fail and spans/segments can be lost or stuck until keys expire. There is no dual read/write path, versioned key prefix, or migration/flush step.

findings.title: Optimized audit-log path selects a paginator that cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: The endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"` together with `OptimizedCursorPaginator` when `optimized_pagination=true` for privileged users. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the model value, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime`, so `build_cursor` raises `TypeError` on the first page, and cursor filtering would compare a datetime column against an integer. Any authorized request entering this new branch will 500 instead of returning audit logs.

findings.title: Negative offsets are still passed to Django QuerySet slicing and raise ValueError
findings.body: The new clamp only applies when `cursor.is_prev` is false: for previous-page cursors the original negative offset is passed through, and `OptimizedCursorPaginator`'s advanced branch (around line 882) explicitly passes `cursor.offset` directly to `queryset[start:stop]`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` rejects negative start/stop with `ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.')`. A crafted cursor such as `value:-1:1`, or the endpoint's new `enable_advanced_features=True` path, therefore produces a 500. The comments claiming Django handles negative slicing are incorrect; offsets need validation/clamping or a `BadPaginationError`.

findings.title: Span buffer hard-codes 1000-span cap and ignores SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans
findings.body: Eviction is now `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(...)` inside the Lua script, while the Python span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`. `SpansBuffer` still exposes `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) and passes nothing to the script, so any configured value is silently ignored and the actual limit is always 1000, which is also one lower than the default. Operators/tests cannot tune the cap, and the Python span-count safety check no longer matches the Lua behavior.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate timestamp scores instead of preserving the latest
findings.body: The script uses `zunionstore set_key, 2, set_key, span_key` (and the same for `parent_key`) without an `AGGREGATE` option. Redis's default is `SUM`, so if a span payload is present in both source sets its score becomes the sum of two `end_timestamp_precise` values rather than the max/latest timestamp. This occurs routinely with at-least-once duplicate/reprocessed spans: a duplicate child is re-added under its parent key and then merged into the destination where the first copy already exists. Since `ZPOPMIN` later uses the score to decide which spans to evict, duplicated spans can be moved to the wrong end of the ordering and be kept or evicted incorrectly. Use `AGGREGATE MAX` or otherwise define duplicate-score handling.

findings.title: No test exercises the new ZPOPMIN eviction path
findings.body: All buffer tests still use only a handful of spans, so the new >1000-span eviction path is completely untested. There is no coverage for the cap being enforced, eviction ordering by `end_timestamp_precise`, retention of a root/segment span, or cleanup/redirect behavior for evicted spans. A regression here silently drops span data, so a test with more than 1000 spans should verify the resulting segment contents and Redis key cleanup.

findings.title: New OptimizedCursorPaginator and audit-log branch have no tests
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a new ~90-line paginator used by the audit-log endpoint, but no test instantiates it or calls the endpoint with `optimized_pagination=true`. Basic coverage would have caught both the datetime `TypeError` and the negative-offset `ValueError`. Add tests for first/next/prev pages, forged negative offsets, and the audit-log optimized path.

findings.title: Redirect-chain traversal limit reduced from 10,000 to 1,000
findings.body: The loop that resolves parent redirects was changed from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`, removing the comment that documented the old limit. If a trace's span-buffer redirect chain is deeper than 1000, the loop stops at an intermediate span id, so the current span is attached to the wrong buffer and segments can be split or duplicated. This is an abrupt behavior change unrelated to the eviction work and has no test; either restore the old bound or justify and test the new one.
